result.title: Actor-Predictor Architecture for Reinforcement Learning with Formal Specification Objectives
result.summary: One fundamental challenge in reinforcement learning (RL) is enforcing temporal safety constraints, such as satisfying formal specifications. Existing methods often transform logic formulas into automata for state augmentation and reward shaping. However, this approach assumes that automaton construction is both feasible and tractable, which limits its applicability to small specifications and linear temporal logic (LTL). This paper proposes Actor-Predictor, a framework that learns a surrogate representation of logic progress without explicitly constructing an automaton. The predictor continuously estimates whether a partial trajectory will satisfy the formal specification in a later step, and its learned features are provided as auxiliary inputs to the actor, which is then optimized using GRPO and RWR. We show theoretically that, under sufficient predictive accuracy, the learned representation is equivalent to the automaton state. Experiments on grid world and robotic tasks in Isaac Lab demonstrate that Actor-Predictor outperforms automaton-based baselines on LTL-constrained tasks. It also performs well on non-regular formal specifications, such as $(a^n b^n)$, for which finite-automaton-based approaches are not applicable.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 Actor-Predictor 框架，用预测器学习形式规范进度的替代表示，并将学到的特征作为 actor 的辅助输入，从而避免显式构造自动机。
AI.relevance_reason: 其通过预测未来是否满足规范来学习紧凑状态表示，可供核查 LVR 中推理状态是否应编码任务进度，以及预测式辅助监督如何影响策略对 latent 的使用；但任务域属 RL 与机器人控制，与 VLM 推理的联系仍需判断。
